question.text: Per the chapter, a Category III AIF may issue DIFFERENT Classes of Units to differentiate investors based on:

answer.text: Quantum and time period of Commitments, and their proportion to Total Fund Corpus

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'A Category III AIF may have differential rights assigned to a specific group of investors, or a class of investors, based on quantum of Commitments, the time period for such commitments made by a class of investors and the proportion of such Commitments to the Total Fund Corpus.' The Trap: Nationality/age/religion are not permissible classification grounds under AIF regulations. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B and XIX-C test class-of-units structure. XIX-A/XIX-D use similar logic for Cat I/II. Manager's Pro-Tip: When designing A1/A2/B1/C1 classes, document the commitment-tier rationale in the PPM so SEBI inspections don't view the scheme as discriminatory. 'Priority distribution' waterfalls are now explicitly banned - keep the differential pure-fee, not pure-returns.
